text:
olivia: Heads-up — I'm bringing up the new reranker (distil-cross-encoder-q8) on the eval infra. Need a quick alignment on which relevance metrics to gate on for rollout: NDCG@10 vs MRR@10? Also any quirks for dataset selection or query/doc formatting we should standardize?

matt: For rerankers I'd pick NDCG@10 as primary (captures graded relevance and position). MRR@10 is useful as a secondary signal for exact-first-hit scenarios like QA. Also report NDCG@3 and Recall@100 for completeness.

kai: Dataset-wise: MS MARCO dev (passage) + TREC DL (19/20) + our in-house product queries. Make sure we run the long-tail subset too. For formatting, canonicalize to `title [SEP] body` (literal token ` [SEP] `) — models seem sensitive to title position. Also normalize whitespace and strip boilerplate footers. Truncate doc to 512 tokens with a hard cutoff on the body only.

sara: Quick Q on quantization: we'll test q8 vs q4_0. Do we expect metric drift from int4 quant? If so what's our statistical plan?

olivia: Early smoke run: q8 baseline -> NDCG@10 0.761, MRR@10 0.668. q4_0 drop to NDCG@10 0.752, MRR@10 0.662 (single-run numbers). Command used:```bash
./eval_runner --model distil-cross-encoder-q8 --dataset msmarco_dev --format "title [SEP] body" --truncate 512 --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10
```

eval-bot: job 3412 finished: ran eval for distil-cross-encoder-q8 q4_0 vs q8. Attached diff: https://redwood.internal/evals/3412 (summary: ndcg10 delta -0.009, p≈0.03 bootstrap) :warning:

matt: Small drop but borderline. Use paired bootstrap to estimate CI, run 3 random seeds (shuffle order / batching seed), and compute per-query paired diffs. For rollout gate, let's use: require NDCG@10 drop > 0.005 AND p < 0.01 to block. Otherwise consider A/B with canary.

kai: Another gotcha: query formatting can change results as much as quantization. In a quick A/B I swapped to `body [SEP] title` and NDCG@10 improved +0.008. So canonicalization is critical — wonky tokenization + leading stopwords matter. Also watch for html-escaped text (`&`) vs raw. Add a preprocessing step to normalize HTML entities.

sara: Good point — we should freeze the preprocessing pipeline in the eval infra. Any objections to creating a 'canonicalization' fixture that tests run must pass? :thumbsup:

olivia: No objections. Plan: 1) freeze preprocess (whitespace, HTML unescape, remove common footers), 2) run full suite: ms_marco_dev + trec_dl19 + trec_dl20 + inhouse_longtail, 3 seeds each, compute NDCG@3/10, MRR@10, Recall@100, paired bootstrap p-values, and save per-query diffs. I'll schedule runs tonight and share plot artifacts.

matt: Also export top-k examples where model disagree to manual eval set (50 queries) — helps root cause (tokenization vs model precision). If quantization is the issue we should see consistent rank-swaps on long passages.

eval-bot: noted. scheduled evals: 3414,3415,3416 (msmarco/trec/inhouse) :spiral_calendar: 

kai: I'll add the canonicalization fixture to eval infra and a small unit test that checks no-ops for already-clean docs. Then we can be confident comparisons are apples-to-apples.

olivia: Perfect — will post results + per-query CSV when runs finish. Thanks everyone. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
